To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
hsp90 alpha is specifically localized to myoD-expressing cells in the zebrafish embryo.
the zebrafish gene hsp90 alpha is expressed in cells that express myoD and that the expression of the hspa gene is down regulated in differentiated muscle.
hsp90 alpha expression in zebrafishes is specific to cells that express myoD and is down-regulated along with myo D in differentiated trunk muscles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the function and regulation of hsp90 in the developing embryo.
the identification of the genes involved in the regulation of the heat shock response.
understanding the molecular mechanisms by which the hsp90 family functions to control the activity of specific signalling molecules and transcriptional regulators during vertebrate development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hsp 90 alpha gene plays an important role during the process of myoD mediated myogenesis.
the hsp 90alpha gene plays a specific and important role in the normal development of the myogenic cells of the trunk and fins of the zebrafish embryo.
hsp90alpha plays a specific role during myogenesis and also has a general protective role against environmental stress.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hsp90 alpha is a muscle-specific molecular chaperone.
the Hsp90alpha protein may play a role during myogenesis and in protection from stress.
the hsp70 and hsp90 genes have different functions during the development of the vertebrate nervous system.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the hsp 90 alpha gene is expressed in the same cells as myoD and the expression of the h90a gene decreases when myoD expression does, but not when the muscle specific gene alpha tropomyosine is expressed.
the expression pattern of hsp90 alpha in zebrafis embryos suggests that the gene is involved in myogenesis.
the hsp 90 alpha gene plays specific role in the process myogenesis.
